restrooms_city.rule: Tacoma Municipal Code 1.29.180 (Ordinance 28563, effective June 1, 2019): a single-occupant restroom in a place of public accommodation, a City facility or a facility of a taxing district (county, port, school district, park district and so on) in Tacoma may not be restricted to one sex or gender identity and must carry a sign saying so; existing gendered signs had to be replaced. Tacoma's building code repeats it for new work: TMC 2.02.202 replaces the signage section (IBC 2902.4) and sends single-occupant rooms to TMC 1.29.180. No Tacoma rule on shared (multi-user) all-gender rooms was found; the state rule (WAC 51-50-2902, subsection 2902.2.2) applies.
restrooms_city.quote: Single-occupant restrooms shall not be restricted to a specific sex or gender identity and shall use appropriate signage to indicate such restrooms are designated for use by any person, regardless of sex or gender identity. Entities covered by this ordinance shall replace existing restrictive-gender-use signage for single-occupant public restrooms with signage indicating that such restrooms can be used by any person, regardless of sex or gender identity.
restrooms_city.definition_quote: "Single-occupant public restroom" means any toileting facility that is designed for use and can be used only by a single individual at a time and/or by a single individual assisted by another individual, located in a facility of the City, a facility of a taxing district located in Tacoma, or a place of public accommodations in the City as defined by TMC 1.29.040.
restrooms_city.building_code_quote: 2902.4 Signage. Required public facilities shall be provided with signs that designate the sex for separate facilities or indicate all-gender facilities. Single-occupant toilet facilities shall be provided with signs compliant with TMC 1.29.180. Signs shall be readily visible and located near the entrance to each toilet facility. Signs for accessible toilet facilities shall also comply with IBC Section 1112.
restrooms_city.enforcement_quote: The requirements of this subsection shall be enforced and violations penalized pursuant to Chapter 1.82 TMC.
restrooms_city.note: Read in the ordinances as passed (Tacoma's Legistar files). The City Clerk's revision table lists 'December 4, 2018 28563 Adds 1.29.180' and no later change to 1.29.180 through 01/2026; the live section on eCode could not be opened.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Tacoma job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material for a damp climate and see the Tacoma rules that apply.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Tacoma schools, clinics, restaurants and port and industrial buildings, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.fire_bullet: - **Fire safety:** Washington's building rules, which Tacoma enforces, require solid plastic (HDPE) partitions to pass a fire test. Ask for the fire-rated version.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Washington sets the number of toilets by how many people use the building, and Tacoma applies the state count without changes. The table below shows what that means. Tacoma Planning and Development Services issues the plumbing permits as well as the building permits.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Tacoma requires a permit for most construction work unless it is on the city's exempt list. The list covers "similar finish work" and movable partitions up to 5 feet 9 inches high, without naming toilet partitions, so ask Tacoma Planning and Development Services (253-591-5030) whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** in Tacoma, a one-person restroom in a business open to the public, a city building or another public agency's building must be open to anyone and signed that way. That covers existing restrooms as well as new ones. Under state rules, a shared all-gender room is allowed if every toilet and urinal is in its own compartment with full-height walls and a door that locks from the inside.
page.stalls_intro: Tacoma uses Washington's count, which goes by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. It isn't the number of staff or of visitors in a day. Half are counted as men and half as women. Every toilet needs a stall. Washington sets its own count for schools, with more toilets for girls than for boys. Urinals are optional and may stand in for most of the men's toilets.
page.stalls_after: Small businesses may be allowed one shared restroom: up to 25 people in an office and up to 30 in a restaurant. At least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible. Confirm your project with Tacoma Planning and Development Services.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, the building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor and a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet. A school is counted at one student per 100 square feet of the whole building. Your architect or Tacoma Planning and Development Services sets the final number.
extra_rule_bullets: - **Rule update planned for May 3, 2027:** Washington's code council plans to bring in the next edition of the state building and plumbing rules on that date, and Tacoma applies state updates on the day they take effect.
page.install_rule: Washington requires every construction contractor to register with the Department of Labor & Industries (L&I). Tacoma adds its own business license: the general contractor and every subcontractor working on a Tacoma job site need one, and the city checks licensing when it issues a building permit. Look a contractor up on the L&I website before you hire. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: In Tacoma that contractor needs a Washington L&I registration and a City of Tacoma business license.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** Washington requires the state-set wage on every public job, with no minimum project size. The Department of Labor & Industries publishes the current Pierce County carpenter rate in its online wage lookup. Where federal money is in the project, the federal rate for a carpenter on building work in Pierce County is $63.98 an hour plus $19.13 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 10.5% in Tacoma: 6.5% state and 4% local.
page.buyers_extra: - **Port terminals, marine shops and waterfront parks:** solid plastic or phenolic for unheated restrooms and rooms open to outside air.
